what: Random draws – threefry only, never R’s own RNG
title: CLAUDE.md
text: Every C++-level random draw goes rxode2’s per-thread, seeded threefry engine (rxNormEng(mean, sd) / rxUnifEng(low, hi), rxode2ptr.h), NEVER R’s RNG (R::rnorm, R::runif, R::rbeta, R::rgamma, unif_rand(), norm_rand(), GetRNGstate()/PutRNGstate(), R-level set.seed() call seed subsequent R::r* draw). makes fit reproducible given control seed=, independent OpenMP thread scheduling R’s ambient/global RNG state, safe draw inside OpenMP-parallel region – R’s RNG API safe call non-main thread. rxNormEng/rxUnifEng exist per-thread draws; distribution engine cover directly (Beta, Gamma, chi-square, truncated normal, …) built inverse-CDF – feed one rxUnifEng(0.0, 1.0) draw matching DETERMINISTIC R::q* quantile function (R::qbeta, R::qgamma, R::qnorm, …). R::p*/R::q* (CDF/quantile, RNG state touched) fine everywhere, including inside OpenMP regions – R::r* (draws) GetRNGstate()/PutRNGstate() banned. See imp.cpp’s impChisqQuantile() npb.cpp’s npbRbeta() pattern. Seed fresh, iteration/chain/group-mixed value (setRxThreadId(0) + nmSetSeedEng1(seed), nmMcmcRng.h) every SERIAL batch draws, rather letting one engine stream free-run across whole fit. subject solve reseeds shared engine mid-solve (setSeedEng1(getRxSeed1()+id) per subject – nmMcmcRng.h’s top comment) whenever runs two draw batches, unconditionally reseeding every batch means batch’s draws depend solve engine , without track/restore state. See saem.cpp’s _saemSeedDoMcmc/_saemSeedCensAug npb.cpp’s npbSeedEng seed-mixing convention – multiplicatively fold EVERY index identifies batch (bare += two indices collides whenever sum value; caused real bug, see _saemSeedCensAug’s history). nmMcmcRng.h’s nmRngGuard()/nmRestoreMcmcSeed() alternative stream must survive ACROSS inner-likelihood call rather freshly reseeded (e.g. do_mcmc’s proposal + acceptance-uniform draws, drawn candidate solved). Truncated-normal draws – src/truncNorm.h. truncated-normal draw (SAEM’s censored-DV data augmentation, saem.cpp’s simCensDv(); CWRES’s censored-observation simulation, censResid.h’s truncnorm()) use rxTruncNorm(l, u) (src/truncNorm.h), plain inverse-CDF draw (qnorm(pnorm(l) + u*(pnorm(u)-pnorm(l)))) – inverse-CDF form loses precision catastrophically l/u SDs 0, exactly regime censored (BQL) observation’s bound often sits . rxTruncNorm() ports rxode2’s rxRmvn machinery (rxthreefry.cpp’s ntail/tn/trandn, Botev (2015) minimax tilting – algorithm backs censResid.h’s truncnorm() CWRES) onto package’s rxNormEng/rxUnifEng engine instead raw sitmo::threefry& reference package access , stays thread-safe reproducible fit’s seed without round-trip R’s SEXP/PROTECT machinery (unsafe call non-main thread) rxRmvn’s R-facing entry point requires.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: emitting rxode2 model text programmatically (e.g. augmented sensitivity models R/foceiCovAnalytic.R / R/foceiGradAnalytic.R, inner/pred models R/focei.R): Name every generated output variable rx_<name>_ (leading rx_, trailing _), matching inner model’s rx_pred_ / rx__sens_..._ convention. Two reasons: (1) user can define model variable plain name (e.g. rvar, predf, f1), un-prefixed generated name can collide silently corrupt model; (2) rxode2 parses top-level x = <constant> initial value (x becomes parameter, dropping solve columns) UNLESS name rx_<name>_ form – keep constant assignment real lhs output column. constant sensitivity (e.g. d(R)/d(eta)=0 additive error) comes back column constant, special-casing needed. Use rx_predf_, rx_f1_<dir>, rx_rvarf_, etc. – never predf, f1_..., rvar, rxPredF (plain rxFoo without trailing _ still parsed init). Use = variable read back (output column solve). Use ~ (suppressed assignment) intermediate compute output – extra = output columns shift positional column layout add solve overhead. Declare theta/eta inputs model covariates (ui$allCovs) param(...) solve parameter order fixed positional (values keyed name, pinning order keeps input layout stable across builds). Covariates supplied event data solve time must still declared param(...). general-likelihood formula referencing DV (dnorm()/t()/cauchy() sugar, literal ll() expression) needs DV declared – needs model-BUILDING side (solve-consuming side) actually supply : DV must listed .configsaem’s inPars (see rxUiGet.saemInParsAndMuRefCovariates, R/saemRxUiGet.R) DV-append step fires, must land model’s first (effective) param() statement, second one appended later (rxode2 silently ignores second param() statement one model – nlmixr2/rxode2#1279).

title: Extending nlmixr2est: custom estimation methods and behavior hooks
text: nlmixr2() dispatches est string nlmixr2Est() S3 generic: estimation environment given class c(est, "nlmixr2Est"), est = "myMethod" calls nlmixr2Est.myMethod(). method needs three pieces: control constructor myMethodControl(...) returning classed list. getValidNlmixrCtl.myMethod(control) – validate/coerce user’s control (called dispatch). nlmixr2Est.myMethod(env, ...) – fit return nlmixr2FitData. time method runs, estimation environment env carries everything need: existing methods best templates – population optimizer bobyqa (R/bobyqa.R) simplest, saem/focei show full pattern. Skeleton: Optional method attributes (mirroring built-ins) advertise capabilities dispatcher, e.g. attr(nlmixr2Est.myMethod, "covPresent") <- TRUE. nlmixr2AllEst() lists every registered method, package loaded est = "myMethod" available like built-.
code: myMethodControl <- function(maxeval = 1000L, ...) {   .ctl <- list(maxeval = as.integer(maxeval), ...)   class(.ctl) <- "myMethodControl"   .ctl }  #' @exportS3Method nlmixr2est::getValidNlmixrCtl getValidNlmixrCtl.myMethod <- function(control) {   .ctl <- control[[1]]   if (is.null(.ctl)) .ctl <- myMethodControl()   if (!inherits(.ctl, "myMethodControl")) {     stop("est = 'myMethod' needs control = myMethodControl(...)", call. = FALSE)   }   .ctl }  #' @exportS3Method nlmixr2est::nlmixr2Est nlmixr2Est.myMethod <- function(env, ...) {   .ui   <- env$ui   .data <- env$data   .ctl  <- env$control   ## ... run the fit, build the result ...   ## return an nlmixr2FitData (see nlmixr2CreateOutputFromUi / the existing methods) }

title: Extending nlmixr2est: custom estimation methods and behavior hooks
text: Sometimes want new est; want model fit standard estimator transparently something extra. example, nlmixr2nn lets model contains neural-network term fit est = "focei" trains network side effect – est = "nn". Register interceptor – function(env) consulted top nlmixr2Est(), standard method dispatches: Returning NULL declines – next interceptor, ordinary method, runs. Returning fit claims estimation. Interceptors re-entrancy guarded: claimed interceptor runs, interceptors suppressed, may call nlmixr2() internally (e.g. requested est) get ordinary method. Register package’s .onLoad() removeEstInterceptor("myPkg") .onUnload().
code: nlmixr2est::registerEstInterceptor("myPkg", function(env) {   if (!shouldClaim(env$ui)) return(NULL)         # decline -> normal fit proceeds   ## claim it: do the work and return a finalized nlmixr2FitData   runMyThing(env) })

title: Extending nlmixr2est: custom estimation methods and behavior hooks
text: deepest hook lets compiled plugin add terms FOCEi/SAEM objective fit – per observation, inside parallel subject loop, R callback (R thread-safe). nlmixr2nn feeds network’s objective cotangents running FOCEi fit. nlmixr2est exposes registry C callables via function-pointer table (nlmixr2est::.nlmixr2estLikContribPtrs()), consumed downstream header inst/include/nlmixr2estLikContrib.h. contributor supplies plain-C entry points (per-subject begin/obs/end bundle /EM per-subject log-likelihood) read per-observation prediction f, residual variance R, dv, add accumulators (llik, dLL/deta, …). Registration via nlmixrRegisterLikContrib() / nlmixrRegisterEmLik(); registry cycled series, several packages can contribute . registry holds raw function pointers, lifecycle matters directions: install pointer table every .onLoad() (reloaded nlmixr2est hands back new addresses), unregister every bundle .onUnload() – nlmixr2est tell DLL gone away, bundle left behind called next objective evaluation. C-linkage API rather R one – see inst/include/nlmixr2estLikContrib.h exact struct nlmixr2nn package (src/*Contrib.c) worked consumer. mechanism follows rxode2’s function-pointer-table convention described rxode2 hooks article.

title: Copilot instructions for nlmixr2est
text: Purpose - Provide concise guidance future Copilot sessions repository (R package C++ sources). Build, test, lint commands - Load package (compiles C/C++): devtools::load_all() - Run full test suite: devtools::test() - Run single test file (example): testthat::test_file(“tests/testthat/test-focei-1.R”) - Build documentation (regenerates NAMESPACE): devtools::document() - Full R CMD check: devtools::check() shell: R CMD check . - Note: package NeedsCompilation: yes requires C++17 (see src/Makevars). devtools::load_all() usual dev workflow recompile native code. High-level architecture (big picture) - Entry points: R/nlmixr2.R -> nlmixr2Est() (S3 dispatch). See R/nlmixr2Est.R dispatch table. - Estimation methods: method R file control function (e.g., R/saem.R + R/saemControl.R, R/focei.R + R/foceiControl.R). - UI → rxode2 pipeline: model UI objects translated rxode2 via R/rxPipeline.R method-specific RxUiGet handlers (R/saemRxUiGet.R, R/splitModelRxUiGet.R, R/nlmeRxUiGet.R). - Pre-processing hooks: R/hook.R registers pre-processing steps. Implementations live R/preProcess.R (bounded transforms, covariates, data/ui validation, zero-omega handling, literal fix processing). - Core numerical layer: C++ src/ (saem.cpp, nlm.cpp, inner.cpp, cwres.cpp, nearPD.cpp, etc.). expose R interfaces via Rcpp exports (RcppExports.cpp / R/RcppExports.R). - Post-fit accessors: Fits nlmixr2FitData objects; accessors lazy computations implemented R/nmObjGet*.R addCwres()/addNpde(). - Tests fixtures: helper-zzz-fits.R pre-fits models stores .rds fixtures tests/testthat/fixtures avoid re-running long estimations. Key conventions repository-specific patterns - “mu2” (mu-referencing): Special handling detection R/mu2.R. SAEM optimizations depend mu-referencing; validate via mu2 code tests. - Preprocess hooks: Use R/hook.R add/remove pre-processing logic. Search preProcess* files see available hooks. - Control objects: sharedControl() centralizes options common estimators; method-specific control functions delegate . - Native code workflow: C++ changes require recompilation via devtools::load_all() (C++17, see src/Makevars). Pay attention Rcpp Armadillo/Eigen usage. - Tests: Many tests rely cached fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures). adding tests require long fits, add fixtures avoid CI slowness. - Naming: Estimation methods map 1:1 R/*.R files (saem.R, focei.R, fo.R, nlm.R, etc.). Look understand behavior control options. One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. nAGQ Number Gauss-Hermite adaptive quadrature points. `0` disables AGQ; `1` equivalent Laplace. Cost grows quickly ETAs: EBE found, expect `nAGQ^neta` (even `nAGQ`) `(nAGQ^neta)-1` (odd `nAGQ`) additional evaluations per subject. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` interaction boolean, Interaction term model, case default `TRUE`; adaptive quadrature, normal distribution Hessian calculated foce() approximation agqLow lower bound adaptive quadrature log-likelihood. default -Inf; original nlmixr's gnlmm -700. agqHi upper bound adaptive quadrature log-likelihood.  default Inf; original nlmixr's gnlmm 400.

title: Control for bobyqa estimation method in nlmixr2 — bobyqaControl
text: npt Number points quadratic approximation objective; must `[n+2, (n+1)(n+2)/2]`. Defaults `min(n*2, n+2)`. rhobeg Initial trust region radius (`rhoend`, must satisfy `0 < rhoend < rhobeg`). Defaults `min(0.95, 0.2*max(abs(par)))`; adjusted upward smaller `abs(upper-lower)/2`. rhoend Final trust region radius.  `NULL` (default) derived `sigdig` way `foceiControl()` (`10^(-sigdig)`); otherwise minqa `1e-6*rhobeg` default applies. iprint Controls amount printing (`0`=none, `1`=start/end , `2`=new rho, `3`=every function evaluation, `>3`=every `iprint` evaluations). SE  %RSE Back-transformed(95%CI) #> E0  -0.579 0.115  19.8 -0.579 (-0.803, -0.354) #> Em    8.61  3.93  45.6      8.61 (0.915, 16.3) #> E50   4.00  1.36  34.1       4.00 (1.33, 6.67) #> g     2.00 FIXED FIXED                    2.00 #>   #>   Covariance Type ($covMethod): r #>   Censoring ($censInformation): No censoring #>  #> ── Fit Data (object is a modified tibble): ── #> # A tibble: 1,000 × 5 #>   ID      TIME    DV  IPRED      v #>   <fct>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1 1     0.0564     0 -0.446 -0.577 #> 2 1     0.0595     1 -1.02  -0.577 #> 3 1     0.0650     1 -1.02  -0.576 #> # ℹ 997 more rows  # you can also get the bobyqa output with  fit2$bobyqa #> parameter estimates: -0.57863859429345, 8.61091072540098, 3.99816989169562  #> objective: 558.702290191142  #> number of function evaluations: 226  # }

title: Control options for the foce estimation method — foceControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` interaction Interaction term model, case default `FALSE`; changed, use `focei` instead

text: sigdig Optimization significant digits. title: Control options for the iagq estimation method — iagqControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. nAGQ Number Gauss-Hermite adaptive quadrature points. `0` disables AGQ; `1` equivalent Laplace. Cost grows quickly ETAs: EBE found, expect `nAGQ^neta` (even `nAGQ`) `(nAGQ^neta)-1` (odd `nAGQ`) additional evaluations per subject. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` interaction boolean, Interaction term model, case default `TRUE`; adaptive quadrature, normal distribution Hessian calculated foce() approximation agqLow lower bound adaptive quadrature log-likelihood. default -Inf; original nlmixr's gnlmm -700. agqHi upper bound adaptive quadrature log-likelihood.  default Inf; original nlmixr's gnlmm 400. muModel Selects regression variant; `iagqControl()` always `"irls"` changed – use `magqControl()` closed-form OLS variant.

title: Control options for the ifoce estimation method — ifoceControl

title: Control options for the ifoce estimation method — ifoceControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` interaction Interaction term model, case default `FALSE`; changed, use `ifocei` instead muModel Selects regression variant; `ifoceControl()` always `"irls"` changed – use `mfoceControl()` closed-form OLS variant.

title: Control options for the ifoce estimation method — ifoceControl
text: ifoceControl object

title: Control options for the ifoce estimation method — ifoceControl
text: `mfocei`/`ifocei` (related) methods apply mu2+ covariate hooks, expand algebraic mu-referenced covariate expressions (e.g. `cl.wt*log(WT/70)`) estimable mu-referenced parameters split covariates non-time-varying (absorbed phi term) time-varying (kept `beta` regressors).  Calling `focei` directly apply hooks, methods can estimate mu-referenced models plain `focei` – genuine difference calling e.g. `est="mfocei"` `est="focei"`. mu-referenced population thetas – without covariates – profiled outer optimizer -C++ regression (intercept-covariate-free pairs), outer gradients calculated non-mu-referenced parameters (residual errors, omegas, non-mu thetas).  Bounded mu-referenced parameters regression-updated update clamped bounds (clamp reported fit note); user-fixed (`fix()`) mu thetas stay regression.

title: Control options for the ifocei estimation method — ifoceiControl
text: Mu-referenced-FOCEI-family reweighted-regression (`"irls"`) variant FOCEI; see `foceiControl(muModel=)`.

title: Control options for the ifocei estimation method — ifoceiControl
code: ifoceiControl(sigdig = 3, ..., muModel = c("irls", "lin", "none"))

title: Control options for the ifocei estimation method — ifoceiControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` muModel Selects regression variant; `ifoceiControl()` always `"irls"` changed – use `mfoceiControl()` closed-form OLS variant.

title: Control options for the ifocei estimation method — ifoceiControl

title: Control options for the ifocei estimation method — ifoceiControl
text: `mfocei`/`ifocei` (related) methods apply mu2+ covariate hooks, expand algebraic mu-referenced covariate expressions (e.g. `cl.wt*log(WT/70)`) estimable mu-referenced parameters split covariates non-time-varying (absorbed phi term) time-varying (kept `beta` regressors).  Calling `focei` directly apply hooks, methods can estimate mu-referenced models plain `focei` – genuine difference calling e.g. `est="mfocei"` `est="focei"`. mu-referenced population thetas – without covariates – profiled outer optimizer -C++ regression (intercept-covariate-free pairs), outer gradients calculated non-mu-referenced parameters (residual errors, omegas, non-mu thetas).  Bounded mu-referenced parameters regression-updated update clamped bounds (clamp reported fit note); user-fixed (`fix()`) mu thetas stay regression.

title: Control iteration-time print formatting — iterPrintControl
text: Bundles options controlling iteration progress output emitted `nlmixr2` estimators. Pass `print` argument `*Control()` function; scalar form (`print = N`) still works wrapped `iterPrintControl()` internally.

title: Control iteration-time print formatting — iterPrintControl
code: iterPrintControl(   every = 1L,   ncol = NULL,   headerEvery = NULL,   useColor = NULL,   simple = FALSE )

title: Control iteration-time print formatting — iterPrintControl
text: every Integer. Print one iteration row every `every` parameter evaluations; `0` suppresses output. Defaults `1L`. ncol Integer `NULL`. Parameter columns per row wrapping. `NULL` (default) uses `floor((getOption("width") - 23) / 12)`. headerEvery Integer `NULL`. Re-emit column header every `headerEvery` parameter-print events; `0` prints fit start. `NULL` (default) uses `10L`. useColor Logical (`NULL`) emit ANSI bold/color escapes iteration print. `NULL` (default) defers [crayon::has_color()]. simple Logical. `TRUE`, print single row per iteration, suppressing unscaled (`U`) / back-transformed (`X`) rows. Defaults `FALSE`.

title: Control iteration-time print formatting — iterPrintControl
text: list validated, defaulted iteration-print   options.  class `"iterPrintControl"` outer `*Control()`   functions can distinguish pre-built object scalar   `print = N`.

title: Control options for the Laplace estimation method — laplaceControl
text: control options adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature likelihood.  Note nAGQ=1 Laplace method.

title: Control options for the Laplace estimation method — laplaceControl
code: laplaceControl(sigdig = 3, ..., nAGQ = 1)

title: Control options for the Laplace estimation method — laplaceControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` nAGQ Number Gauss-Hermite adaptive quadrature points. `0` disables AGQ; `1` equivalent Laplace. Cost grows quickly ETAs: EBE found, expect `nAGQ^neta` (even `nAGQ`) `(nAGQ^neta)-1` (odd `nAGQ`) additional evaluations per subject.

title: Control options for the magq estimation method — magqControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. nAGQ Number Gauss-Hermite adaptive quadrature points. `0` disables AGQ; `1` equivalent Laplace. Cost grows quickly ETAs: EBE found, expect `nAGQ^neta` (even `nAGQ`) `(nAGQ^neta)-1` (odd `nAGQ`) additional evaluations per subject. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` interaction boolean, Interaction term model, case default `TRUE`; adaptive quadrature, normal distribution Hessian calculated foce() approximation agqLow lower bound adaptive quadrature log-likelihood. default -Inf; original nlmixr's gnlmm -700. agqHi upper bound adaptive quadrature log-likelihood.  default Inf; original nlmixr's gnlmm 400. muModel Selects regression variant; `magqControl()` always `"lin"` changed – use `iagqControl()` IRLS variant.

title: Control options for the mfoce estimation method — mfoceControl
text: `mfocei`/`ifocei` (related) methods apply mu2+ covariate hooks, expand algebraic mu-referenced covariate expressions (e.g. `cl.wt*log(WT/70)`) estimable mu-referenced parameters split covariates non-time-varying (absorbed phi term) time-varying (kept `beta` regressors).  Calling `focei` directly apply hooks, methods can estimate mu-referenced models plain `focei` – genuine difference calling e.g. `est="mfocei"` `est="focei"`. mu-referenced population thetas – without covariates – profiled outer optimizer -C++ regression (intercept-covariate-free pairs), outer gradients calculated non-mu-referenced parameters (residual errors, omegas, non-mu thetas).  Bounded mu-referenced parameters regression-updated update clamped bounds (clamp reported fit note); user-fixed (`fix()`) mu thetas stay regression.

title: Control options for the mfocei estimation method — mfoceiControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` muModel Selects regression variant; `mfoceiControl()` always `"lin"` changed – use `ifoceiControl()` IRLS variant.

title: Control options for the mfocei estimation method — mfoceiControl
text: `mfocei`/`ifocei` (related) methods apply mu2+ covariate hooks, expand algebraic mu-referenced covariate expressions (e.g. `cl.wt*log(WT/70)`) estimable mu-referenced parameters split covariates non-time-varying (absorbed phi term) time-varying (kept `beta` regressors).  Calling `focei` directly apply hooks, methods can estimate mu-referenced models plain `focei` – genuine difference calling e.g. `est="mfocei"` `est="focei"`. mu-referenced population thetas – without covariates – profiled outer optimizer -C++ regression (intercept-covariate-free pairs), outer gradients calculated non-mu-referenced parameters (residual errors, omegas, non-mu thetas).  Bounded mu-referenced parameters regression-updated update clamped bounds (clamp reported fit note); user-fixed (`fix()`) mu thetas stay regression.

title: Control options for the mfocep (mu-referenced FOCE+) estimation method — mfocepControl
text: Mu-referenced-FOCEI-family closed-form-regression (`"lin"`) variant FOCE+ (interaction, live conditional residual variance R); `mfoce` `foce = "foce+"` forced (see `foceiControl(foce=)`).

title: Control options for the mfocep (mu-referenced FOCE+) estimation method — mfocepControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiControl()` interaction Interaction term model, case default `FALSE`; changed, use `mfocei` instead muModel Selects regression variant; `mfocepControl()` always `"lin"` changed – use `ifocepControl()` IRLS variant. foce FOCE residual-variance mode; `mfocepControl()` always `"foce+"` changed – use `mfoceControl()` `"nonmem"`

title: Control options for the mfocep (mu-referenced FOCE+) estimation method — mfocepControl
text: mfocepControl object

title: Control options for the mfocep (mu-referenced FOCE+) estimation method — mfocepControl
text: `mfocei`/`ifocei` (related) methods apply mu2+ covariate hooks, expand algebraic mu-referenced covariate expressions (e.g. `cl.wt*log(WT/70)`) estimable mu-referenced parameters split covariates non-time-varying (absorbed phi term) time-varying (kept `beta` regressors).  Calling `focei` directly apply hooks, methods can estimate mu-referenced models plain `focei` – genuine difference calling e.g. `est="mfocei"` `est="focei"`. mu-referenced population thetas – without covariates – profiled outer optimizer -C++ regression (intercept-covariate-free pairs), outer gradients calculated non-mu-referenced parameters (residual errors, omegas, non-mu thetas).  Bounded mu-referenced parameters regression-updated update clamped bounds (clamp reported fit note); user-fixed (`fix()`) mu thetas stay regression.

title: C++ implementation of Matrix's nearPD — nmNearPD
text: x numeric \(n \times n\) approximately positive     definite matrix, typically approximation correlation     covariance matrix.  x symmetric (    ensureSymmetry false), symmpart(x) used. keepDiag logical, generalizing corr: TRUE,     resulting matrix diagonal     (diag(x)) input matrix. do2eigen logical indicating     posdefify() eigen step applied     result Higham algorithm. doDykstra logical indicating Dykstra's correction     used; true default.  false, algorithm basically     direct fixpoint iteration     \(Y_k = P_U(P_S(Y_{k-1}))\). .values logical; TRUE, result just     vector eigenvalues approximating matrix. ensureSymmetry logical; symmetrizes `x` via symmpart unless already symmetric. Beware: setting FALSE asymmetric input typically nonsense. eig.tol defines relative positiveness eigenvalues compared     largest one, \(\lambda_1\). Eigenvalues \(\lambda_k\)     treated zero \(\lambda_k / \lambda_1 \le eig.tol\). conv.tol convergence tolerance Higham algorithm. posd.tol tolerance enforcing positive definiteness (    final posdefify step do2eigen TRUE). maxit maximum number iterations allowed. trace logical integer specifying convergence monitoring     traced.

title: C++ implementation of Matrix's nearPD — nmNearPD
text: unlike matrix package, simply returns nearest   positive definite matrix

title: C++ implementation of Matrix's nearPD — nmNearPD
text: implements algorithm Higham (2002), (  do2eigen true) forces positive definiteness using code   posdefify.  algorithm Knol ten   Berge (1989) (implemented ) general   allows constraints (1) fix rows (columns) matrix   (2) force smallest eigenvalue certain value. Note setting corr = TRUE just sets diag(.) <- 1   within algorithm. Higham (2002) uses Dykstra's correction, version Jens   Oehlschlägel use (accidentally),   still gave reasonable results; simplification, now   used doDykstra = FALSE,   active nearPD() Matrix version 0.999375-40.

title: Control for the npag (nonparametric adaptive grid) method — npagControl
text: points Initial Sobol grid size (support points).  `NULL` (default) picks automatically number support-point dimensions (etas): `max(2028, 512 * n_eta)` – fixed grid (Pmetrics uses 2028) covers low-dimensional model grows sparse can collapse high dimensions, auto size floors 2028 scales per added eta.  Supply integer override. cycles Maximum adaptive-grid cycles. gammaOptimize Use global assay-error multiplier per-cycle warm start overall residual magnitude, folded variance-scale coefficients (`add`/`prop`/`lnorm`).  per-endpoint values, add/prop ratio, transform/autocorrelation parameters come residOptimize.  valid normal endpoints; censoring transform--sides supported.  Unrelated [impmapControl()]'s `gamma`, inflates importance-sampling proposal's variance meaning . residOptimize estimate residual-error thetas (every endpoint's `add`/`prop`/`lnorm`, transform `lambda`, `ar`) support points weights held fixed, using bounded minqa::bobyqa EXTENDED LEAST SQUARES objective `sum_obs((f-dv)^2/r + log(r))` posterior-mean etas.  `log(r)` term keeps residual drifting zero flexible support (marginal likelihood reward), giving saem/focei residual; variance scale warm-started per-endpoint moment (additive SD `sqrt(mean(err^2))`, proportional `sqrt(mean((err/f)^2))`, transform- -sides scale).  "alternate" (default) optimizes every cycle (block- coordinate ascent); "final" optimizes converged support; "none" holds initial values.  Fixed residual parameters always held.  residual thetas converge, final adaptive-grid pass re-optimizes support held constant support remains nonparametric MLE (D(F) ~ 0) fitted residual. muExpand estimate non-mu structural fixed-effect parameters (theta eta, e.g. `ke <- exp(tke)`; npag's grid otherwise covers mu-referenced residual/likelihood parameters).  `FALSE` (default) optimizes directly "regressors" residual step – `bobyqa` moves alongside residual parameters, re-deriving posterior-mean etas candidate (eta grid stale-absorb structural shift) – identifies well (e.g. recovering clearance poor start).  available mix() models (ELS step mixture-aware; component parameters held).  `TRUE` instead uses saem-style mu-expansion: inject pseudo-eta (`ke <- exp(tke + eta.tke)`), grid-estimate, recover fixed effect finalization (support-mean folded theta, injected random effect collapsed).  regressor default usually identifies parameters sharply grid. gridWidth support-point box half-width, initial-eta SDs, `gridBounds="auto"` grid (default 4).  narrower box focuses initial Sobol grid plausible region – useful high-dimensional models wide box wastes points near-zero-density support (can collapse fit). gridBounds set initial support-point box: `"auto"` (default) uses `+/- gridWidth * initial eta SD`; `"ini"` uses mu-referenced parameter's ini-block lower/upper bounds finite (else auto); `""` uses ini bounds present auto otherwise.  high-dimensional model, bounded ini estimates + `"ini"` keep grid range. dfScan Size Sobol scan used D(F) global-optimality certificate: `-1` (default) auto-sizes `max(2048, 2 * points)`, `0` skips certificate (`npagDF` `NA`), positive value sets explicit scan size.  scan affect fit, reported certificate; smaller scan faster. cores Number threads used parallel per-subject conditional- likelihood solves.  `NULL` (default) uses current `rxode2` thread count (`rxode2::getRxThreads()`); integer sets thread count fit (restored afterwards).  Results independent thread count. rhoend Final trust-region radius (`rhoend`) inner bounded `bobyqa` fits residual-error thetas cycle.  fixed default `1e-4`, matching optimizer convergence tolerance `10^(-sigdig)` `sigdig = 4` (npag `sigdig`, derived ). gamma, df Declared REJECTED rather partially matched.  `gamma` prefix `gammaOptimize`, without explicit formal R bound `gamma = 2` silently turned assay-error optimisation ; `df` importance-sampling proposal control nonparametric engine never builds.  Passing either error. ... Parameters passed [impmapControl()], shared FOCEI-family   scaffolding (inner MAP problem, mu-referencing, residual error   model, threads).  importance-sampling controls **rejected** rather   accepted: `isample`, `df`, `auto`, `iaccept`, `gamma`, `qr`, `sir`   rest configure proposal density nonparametric engine never   builds, passing one error rather silent -op.  np   control job message names (`nIter` -> `cycles`,   `ctol` -> `rhoend`). Note `gamma` `gammaOptimize`: `gamma` impmap's proposal-variance   inflation (NONMEM `ISCALE`), `gammaOptimize` global assay-error   multiplier residual magnitude.  unrelated, `gamma`   prefix `gammaOptimize`, rejected explicitly stop R's partial   matching silently binding one .

title: Run the NPAG adaptive-grid cycle on a set-up inner problem — npagCycle_

code: npbControl(   points = 50L,   alpha = 1,   burnin = 500L,   nsamp = 500L,   nchains = 1L,   propSd = 0.2,   seed = 42L,   residOptimize = c("alternate", "final", "none"),   cycles = 100L,   gammaOptimize = FALSE,   muExpand = FALSE,   cores = NULL,   rhoend = 1e-04,   gamma,   df,   ... )

title: Control for the npb (nonparametric Bayes) method — npbControl
text: points Stick-breaking truncation level K (number support points). alpha Dirichlet-process concentration parameter. burnin Number burn-Gibbs sweeps. nsamp Number post-burn-Gibbs samples collected. nchains Number independent chains (Gelman-Rubin R-hat convergence reported nchains > 1). propSd Standard deviation Gaussian random-walk MH proposal support-point locations (eta space). seed Random seed sampler. residOptimize estimate residual-error thetas (every endpoint's `add`/`prop`/`lnorm`, transform `lambda`, `ar`) non-mu structural "regressor" theta, sampled mixing distribution held fixed, using bounded `bobyqa` EXTENDED LEAST SQUARES objective (see [npagControl()]; `log(r)` term keeps residual collapsing zero moment warm-start gives saem-style SD).  "alternate" (default) re-fits burn-holds fixed sampling phase (every collected draw shares converged residual scale); "final" holds initial values sampling fits converged draw; "none" holds initial values throughout.  Fixed residual parameters always held.  Unlike npag, npb optimize assay-error multiplier (gamma); residual thetas fit directly. cycles Unused npb (kept control compatibility). gammaOptimize Unused npb (kept control compatibility). muExpand `TRUE`, mu-expand non-mu structural fixed-effect thetas (theta eta) grid-estimable pseudo-etas fit; `FALSE` (default) leaves residual step. cores Number threads used parallel per-subject conditional- likelihood solves Gibbs sweeps.  `NULL` (default) uses current `rxode2` thread count (`rxode2::getRxThreads()`); integer sets thread count fit (restored afterwards).  fixed `seed` fit bit--bit identical regardless thread count. rhoend Final trust-region radius (`rhoend`) inner bounded `bobyqa` fits residual-error thetas.  fixed default `1e-4`, matching optimizer convergence tolerance `10^(-sigdig)` `sigdig = 4` (npb `sigdig`, derived ). gamma, df Declared REJECTED rather partially matched.  `gamma` prefix `gammaOptimize`, without explicit formal R bound `gamma = 2` silently turned assay-error optimisation ; `df` importance-sampling proposal control nonparametric engine never builds.  Passing either error. ... Parameters passed [impmapControl()], shared FOCEI-family scaffolding .  importance-sampling controls **rejected** rather accepted – see [npagControl()] – `cycles` `gammaOptimize`, signature carries `npb` use.  `impSeed` rejected pointing `seed`.

title: Control options for the posthoc estimation method — posthocControl
text: sigdig Optimization significant digits.  One value drives, single consistent formula, inner/outer optimizer convergence tolerance (10^-sigdig), boundary check tolerance (5*10^(-sigdig+1)), ODE solver tolerances: rtol exponent sigdig atol sits three orders , rtol = 10^-sigdig, atol = 10^(-sigdig-3) every solver (stiff, non-stiff auto-switching).  sensitivity (atolSens/rtolSens) tolerances match main solve (outer gradient covariance built ); steady-state (ssAtol/ssRtol) tolerances run one order looser. Keying optimizer 10^-sigdig means converges exactly precision solve supports.  default sigdig = 3 atol = 1e-6, rtol = 1e-3. ... Parameters used default `foceiConrol()` interaction Interaction term model, case default `FALSE`, though can set `TRUE` well. maxOuterIterations ignored, posthoc always sets 0.
